The first verse of the Qur’an is the opening of **Surah Al-Fatiha** (Chapter 1).

**Exact Arabic text:**
> بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ

**Transliteration:**
> Bismillāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīm

**English translation (common rendering):**
> In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

*(Other widely used translations render it as: “In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.”)*

**Surah Al-Ikhlas (112), verse 1**

**Arabic text:**
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ

**English translation:**
Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One"  
*(or: Say: He is Allah, the One)*

This is the opening verse of the chapter, followed by the declaration of His absolute oneness and uniqueness.

That is **Ayat al-Kursi** (the Verse of the Throne), Surah Al-Baqarah (2:255).

**Exact Arabic text:**

اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ

**English translation** (Sahih International):

> Allah — there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

That is the opening of **Surah Ya-Sin** (Chapter 36).

**Arabic text:**
> **يس**

**Transliteration:** *Yā Sīn*

**English translation (Sahih International):**
> **"Ya, Seen."**

*(Also commonly rendered as "Ya Sin.")*

**Note:** These are two of the *huruf muqatta'ah* (disjointed letters) that begin several Qur'anic chapters. Their precise meaning is known to Allah, though classical scholars have suggested they may refer to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or serve as a divine oath/attention-caller. The Surah itself is named after these letters: **Surah Ya-Sin**.

The verse is **Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12)**.

**Arabic text:**
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا ۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَّحِيمٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
“O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.”

*(Note: The verse continues with the command to avoid much suspicion, to not spy, and not to backbite, using the metaphor of eating a dead brother’s flesh to illustrate the repugnance of gossip.)*

The verse is **Surah An-Nur (24:35)** — the famous “Light Verse” (*Ayat al-Nur*).

**Exact Arabic text:**
> ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشْكَوٰةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ ٱلْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيٓءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ ۗ يَهْدِي ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

**English translation** (Sahih International):
> Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star. It is lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if it had not been touched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.

*(Note: The verse is often recited with the preceding verse 24:34, which begins with “And Allah has made for you from yourselves mates…” — together they form the well-known “Light Verse” passage.)*

**Surah Al-‘Asr (103), verse 2**

**Arabic text:**
إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ

**English translation:**
Indeed, mankind is in loss.  
*(Or: Indeed, man is in loss.)*

**Surah Luqman (31), Verse 13**

**Arabic text:**
وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ

**English translation** (Sahih International):
> "And [mention] when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, 'O my son, do not associate partners with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice.'"

*(Other common translations render it similarly, e.g., "O my son, do not set up partners with Allah..." or "do not commit shirk with Allah...")*

This is **Surah Al-Mujadila (58), verse 11**.

**Arabic text:**
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجَالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ انشُزُوا فَانشُزُوا يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ

**English translation** (Sahih International):
> O you who have believed, when it is said to you, "Make room" in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when it is said, "Rise," then rise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.

**Brief context:** The verse instructs believers to spread out and make space in gatherings (rather than crowding together), and to respond respectfully when asked to rise or stand. It promises that Allah will expand their space (in this life and the Hereafter) and elevate the ranks of believers and those granted knowledge.

The verse is **Surah Al-‘Ankabut (29:45)**.

**Arabic text:**
وَاتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ ۚ إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنكَرِ ۗ وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَصْنَعُونَ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
“And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prevents immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do.”

*(Note: The verse is part of a longer passage; the full verse continues with “And argue not with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best…” — but the text above is the complete verse 29:45 as it appears in the Qur’an.)*

**Surah Al-Mutaffifin (83), Verse 1**

**Arabic text (Uthmani script):**
وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ

**Transliteration:**
*Waylun lil-muṭaffifīn*

**English translation (e.g., Sahih International):**
**“Woe to those who give short measure”**  
—or more broadly—**“Woe to the defrauders / cheaters”** (those who cheat in weights, measures, or transactions).

**Context:** This is the opening verse of Surah 83, which condemns merchants and people who deal dishonestly by giving less than what is due when measuring or weighing goods for others, while demanding full measure for themselves.
